speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I need to evaluate your skin lesions for potential oncologic issues; can you describe any new moles, spots, or growths you are noticing? Please tell me about their size, color, shape, and if they have been changing recently.

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details, Mr. Smith. Given your heavy smoking history, age, and the non-healing, crusty nature of the lesions on your penis and finger, we must rule out malignancy. Has either lesion bled spontaneously, ulcerated deeply, or caused significant pain or itching?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (penile and cutaneous).

I have identified two distinct, non-healing, crusty lesions in a high-risk patient with a significant smoking history and failed prior treatments for syphilis and eczema. These clinical features are highly suspicious for malignancy.

REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide dermoscopic or high-resolution photos of the penile and digital lesions for further confirmation.

REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of the penile lesion and the left middle finger lesion.
